verdict.rationale: a-Shell has no web API: the OpenAPI and llms.txt probes return 404. It does ship its own Apple Shortcuts actions, which the docs say give "full control of the Shell". `Execute Command` runs arbitrary command lists and `Put File`/`Get File` move files, and since the UI is itself a command line (config, newWindow, pickFolder and so on are commands), most UI functions are reachable programmatically. Missing for 10: a documented general-purpose API (HTTP or otherwise) beyond Shortcuts, an explicit statement that every UI-only interaction (e.g. GUI pickers) can be driven programmatically, reliable in-extension execution (the docs warn it "won't always work"), and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: a-Shell is compatible with Apple Shortcuts, giving users full control of the Shell.
`Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order.
`Put File` and `Get File` are used to transfer files to and from a-Shell.
